items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 143:1
items.html: (To the question) What is Tifferet in the aspect of being by itself? It is known that Daat is divided into Hesed and Gevura, which are called Tifferet and Yesod. It is also known that the main bearer of this Hochma of the thirty-two paths is the Tifferet, and therefore it is called by the name sun, being the root of all the lights that are revealed after AA, from the aspect of the Upper Essentiality, for the essentiality of AA is sealed in a membrane, and there is no revelation of essentiality from it and below, except through the Hochma of the thirty-two paths. And since the Tifferet is the main bearer of the illumination of this Hochma, therefore it is called by the name sun, meaning, just as the sun is the root of all the lights of this world, so ZA is the root of all the lights that are from AA. However, it is discerned in two aspects: one, when it is by itself, namely, outside the sheath of the screens in the crown of Gevura, when the aspect of its Hochma illuminates in complete revelation. And this does not operate except in the Mochin in the place of their emergence, namely, in the place of the GAR of AA, where Aba and Ima ascended at the time of the coupling. And there is a second aspect, that the Tifferet is clothed in the sheath of the crown of Gevura, and then the Tifferet is also called by the name crown, because it does not serve in its own measure but in the measure of the crown of the Yesod. And it is called by the name "the sun in its sheath," for all the Mochin of the six thousand years are from the aspect of the two crowns, which are the aspect of the sun in its sheath. However, in the future these Mochin will illuminate as they illuminate in the upper Aba and Ima in the place of their emergence, namely, that the Tifferet will illuminate from the aspect of being by itself, outside the sheath, as above. And on this the Sages hinted: "In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring out the sun from its sheath," etc. (Item 81).
